reset.title: Reset asserted at a rising edge
reset.text: Reset wins over read and write. Occupancy becomes zero; empty is true and full is false after the edge.

read_not_empty.title: Read requested while not empty
read_not_empty.text: Remove the oldest word. dout holds that word after the edge.

read_empty.title: Read requested while empty
read_empty.text: Ignore the read. Nothing is consumed and nothing is bypassed.

both_mid.title: Read and write between empty and full
both_mid.text: Accept both. Occupancy stays constant; the old head is read and the new word joins the tail.

both_empty.title: Read and write while empty
both_empty.text: Accept only the write. The new word is not bypassed to dout.

both_full.title: Read and write while full
both_full.text: Accept only the read. The write is ignored even though the read frees a slot.

idle.title: No request
idle.text: Occupancy and stored words are unchanged.

wraparound.title: Wraparound
wraparound.text: Preserve accepted-word ordering and capacity across pointer wraparound.

checks.empty_flag: empty equals (reference occupancy == 0) after every edge
checks.full_flag: full equals (reference occupancy == DEPTH) after every edge
checks.read_data: dout equals the reference head removed by an accepted read

assumptions: Reset is asserted at the first sampled edge; no pre-reset state is claimed.
Later reset pulses are legal and are exercised.
Inputs are driven while the clock is low and held stable through the rising edge.
Two-state digital semantics; X-propagation, timing closure, and synthesized behavior are not checked.
No requirement is imposed on dout unless the preceding edge accepted a read.
Results apply only to the exact instantiated DEPTH and WIDTH.
sampling: Cycle k names a rising edge. Accepted operations come from the reference queue before the edge; reset has priority; flags are checked after the edge; dout is checked only after an accepted read.
